bottleneck: Non-invasive BCIs avoid surgery but pay a brutal physics tax: the skull attenuates electrical signals by 80-90%, smearing the activity of billions of neurons into blurry scalp potentials. Dry-electrode headsets add drift, sweat, and hair interference, driving high return rates for consumer devices and unreliable performance in daily use. The spatial resolution needed for fluent communication or fine motor control is physically unreachable from outside the skull, no matter how clever the algorithms. Signal processing can only recover what the physics preserves.
current_state: Advanced signal processing and high-density EEG squeeze more from scalp signals, but the fundamental resolution gap versus invasive recording persists and is bounded by physics, not engineering effort.

title: Skull attenuation caps non-invasive BCI resolution
why_it_blocks: Safe, surgery-free BCIs are what the mass market and most patients need, yet physics limits them to crude control. The field is stuck choosing between resolution and safety, with no technology bridging the gap.
